THE INTERNATIONAL COMMITTEE FOR THE
ORGANIZATION OF EUROPEAN IMMIGRANTS
IN CHINA

SHANGHAI. 17th November, 1941.

Shanghai Municipal Police,
Special Branch,
SHANGHAI.

Dear Sirs,

On various occasions during the past few months, we have requested the Shanghai Telephone Company to allocate a telephone to one of our staff living in Hongkew, with whom the undersigned, in the case of an emergency, can communicate. The Shanghai Telephone Company has always given the stereotyped reply that they have no instruments, and this inspite of the urgency and necessity of the telephone for the needs of this Committee being represented to them very thoroughly.

As an illustration may I say that yesterday, at about 7 p.m., I was called up by West Hongkew Police Station and informed that there had been a suicide case, to which we had to send a representative at the inquest the following morning, i.e. this morning. I had absolutely no means of communicating with any responsible member of my staff in order to give the necessary emergency instructions, and it was only by telephoning to someone living in the International Settlement and asking him to go out to Hongkew and try to locate a staff member, that I was finally able to make the necessary arrangements.

This state of affairs is an impossible one, and I feel sure that with some good will, the Telephone Company could find one instrument, even if it had to deprive perhaps one or the other of the many exchange shops, which sport from 8 - 9 instruments, of one telephone.

In view of the fact that this Committee works in close co-operation with the SMP and with your Branch, I would appreciate it very much if you would use your influence with the Telephone Company and ask them to instal telephone service at

No. 43 Muirhead Road,
for Mrs. Lisa Altura;

Mrs. Altura's application has been on record for more than 18 months; she is my personal secretary, and I must be able to contact her at all times of the day or night.

Thanking you in anticipation for your good offices,
I am, dear Sirs,
Yours faithfully,
Hon. Secretary.

（左侧手写批注：）
a/c. r?
Sir,
I do not think the Police can interfere on behalf of the I. C. Surely if they explained their case fully to a responsible member of the Telephone Co. they would get favourable consideration?
（印章：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE SPECIAL BRANCH NOV 18 1941）
18/11/41

在华欧洲移民组织国际委员会

上海，1941年11月17日。

上海公共租界工部局警务处，
特别处，
上海。

尊敬的先生们：

在过去几个月中，我们曾多次请求上海电话公司为一名居住在虹口的职员分配一部电话，以便签署人在紧急情况下能与其联系。上海电话公司总是给予千篇一律的答复，称没有设备，尽管我们已向他们非常充分地陈述了本委员会对电话的紧迫性和必要性。

举例来说，昨天下午7点左右，我接到西区虹口警署的电话，告知发生了一起自杀案件，我们需要派一名代表参加次日上午（即今天上午）的验尸听证会。我完全无法与我职员的任何负责人联系以发出必要的紧急指令，最后只有通过打电话给一位住在公共租界的人，请他外出到虹口设法寻找一名职员，我才最终得以做出必要安排。

这种状况是不可接受的，我相信只要电话公司稍加善意，即使不得不从那些拥有8至9部电话的众多交换商店中剥夺其中一两家的一部电话，也能找到一部设备。

鉴于本委员会与上海公共租界工部局警务处及贵处密切合作，如蒙阁下利用对电话公司的影响力，要求他们在以下地址安装电话服务，我将不胜感激：

缪尔黑德路（Muirhead Road）43号，
供丽莎·阿尔图拉（Lisa Altura）夫人使用；

阿尔图拉夫人的申请已备案超过18个月；她是我的私人秘书，我必须能够随时在白天或夜晚与她联系。

预先感谢阁下的斡旋，
此致，
敬礼

荣誉秘书。

（左侧手写批注：）
a/c. r?
先生，
我认为警方不能代表国际委员会（I. C.）进行干预。如果他们向电话公司的负责人充分解释情况，难道不会得到有利的考虑吗？
（印章：上海公共租界工部局警务处特别处 1941年11月18日）
1941年11月18日

编号 17 1-41 2000

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
Misc. File No. 6/40.
Wayside Station,
REPORT
Date March 1st. 1940.

Subject. Disturbance in the Ward Road Camp for German refugees.

Made by D.S. Larby. Forwarded by [Signature]
Officer i/c.

Sir,

At 1.45 p.m. on 1-3-40, a telephone message was received by Wayside Station from Dr. J. Weinberger, in charge of the camp at 138 Ward Road for German refugees, to the effect that a disturbance was taking place among the inmates of this establishment.

A party of Police under Sub-Inspector T. Walker attended and discovered a crowd of some two hundred German Jews holding a meeting to protest the action of the Refugee Committee in arranging for the transfer of fifty unmarried men from the Ward Road Camp to the camp situated at 1090 Pichiang Road, in order to make room for a number of Jewish families moving into the former addresses.

Haranguing the assembly was a German refugee, one Mr. Robert Weishut, 52, s/unemployed, 138 Ward Road, who was indulging in a vehement criticism of the Refugee Committee's proposed actions. Resultant from enquiries, it appears that the above-named individual, who apparently has some pretensions to being a barrister in his native land, has organized at the Ward Road Camp, a "Camp Inmates Association," presumably with the idea of dictating to the Refugee Committee. The influence of this association, however, in view of its sponsor's unstable temperament is not at present expected to expand.

On being advised by the Police to disperse, the meeting did so while Sub-Inspector Walker cautioned Mr. Weishut regarding his future behaviour.

[Signature]
D.S. Larby.

Sen. Det. 1/c.
D.D.O. "D".
D.C. (sp. 4r).

上海公共租界工部局警务处。
杂项档案号 6/40。
路边警亭，
报告
日期 1940年3月1日。

主题：华德路（Ward Road）德籍难民营骚乱。

制作人：侦探警长（D.S.）拉比（Larby）。转发人 [签名]
负责警官。

先生：

1940年3月1日下午1点45分，路边警亭接到华德路138号德籍难民营负责人J. 温伯格（J. Weinberger）博士的电话留言，称该机构收容人员中正在发生骚乱。

由副督察T. 沃克（T. Walker）率领的一队警察到场，发现约有二百名德籍犹太人聚集开会，抗议难民委员会安排将五十名单身男子从华德路难民营转移至毕江路（Pichiang Road）1090号的难民营，以便为搬入原址的若干犹太家庭腾出空间。

向集会人群发表演说的是名为罗伯特·魏舒特（Robert Weishut）的德籍难民，52岁，无业，住华德路138号，他对难民委员会拟采取的行动进行了激烈批评。经查询，上述此人显然在其本国自称具有律师资格，已在华德路难民营组织了一个“难民营住客协会”，推测其意图是对难民委员会发号施令。然而，鉴于其发起者情绪不稳定，预计该协会的影响力目前不会扩大。

经警方劝告解散后，集会人群散去，副督察沃克同时警告魏舒特先生注意其今后的行为。

[签名]
D.S. 拉比。

高级侦探 1/c.
D.D.O. "D".
D.C. (sp. 4r).
